problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-\operatorname{ln}⁡z?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}) & =c \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & ={e}^{c}\end{aligned}
$$

If we let ${e}^{c}={r}^{2},$ we get

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the level surfaces form a family of spheres centered at the origin.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: A family of spheres centered at the origin
